name: Yellowknife Bay
why: Curiosity's first drill holes: mudstone from an ancient freshwater lake that could have supported microbial life
source: NASA/JPL MSL waypoint feed, rover stop at sol 166 (rover parked here for the Sheepbed drilling campaign, sols 125–297)

name: Pahrump Hills
why: Base of Mount Sharp: lake-bed layers of the Murray formation, where the rover first drilled into the mountain
source: NASA/JPL MSL waypoint feed, rover stop at sol 753 (arrival at Pahrump Hills, base of Mount Sharp)

name: Vera Rubin Ridge
why: Hematite-capped ridge mapped from orbit by CRISM. It records groundwater altering old lake sediments
source: NASA/JPL MSL waypoint feed, rover stop at sol 2128 (rover on the ridge, sols 1800–2300)

name: Glen Torridon (clay unit)
why: The most clay-rich rocks Curiosity has drilled, with sulfur-bearing organic molecules: a prime biosignature target
source: Glen Torridon ridges study map centre (PMC9286800); USGS 2022 overview

name: Woodland Bay
why: Clay-bearing outcrop with Vera Rubin Ridge to the northwest and active rippled sand nearby
